'''Muñoz''', officially the '''Science City of Muñoz''' ({{langx|fil|Lungsod Agham ng Muñoz}},<ref>{{cite web |title=SK ng Lungsod Agham ng Muñoz |trans-title=SK (Youth Council) of the Science City of Muñoz |url=https://sciencecityofmunoz.gov.ph/news-and-events/sk-ng-lungsod-agham-ng-munoz/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |publisher=Science City of Muñoz Government |language=fil}}</ref> [[Ilocano language|Ilocano]]: ''Siudad ti Siensia ti Muñoz'', [[Pangasinan language|Pangasinan]]: ''Siyudad ya Siyensiya na Muñoz''), is a [[Cities of the Philippines#Legal classification|component city]] in the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Nueva Ecija]], [[Philippines]]. According to the {{PH wikidata|population_as_of}}, it has a population of {{PH wikidata|population_total}} people.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}}

Originally known as ''Sitio Papaya'', it was renamed Muñoz in 1886 in honor of the Spanish governor Don Francisco Muñoz. In 1913, Executive Order No. 72 declared Muñoz a separate municipality. By virtue of Republic Act No. 8977, signed on November 7, 2000, Muñoz was converted into a component city and became the country's only city with "Science" in its official name.

==Etymology==
The town got its name in honor of Don Francisco Muñoz, being the alcalde mayor and gobernadorcillo. <!--NOTE: Name was acquired in the year 1886, during the time where Muñoz was not yet a city-->

Science City of Muñoz, located in Nueva Ecija, Philippines, is known for its agricultural research and scientific institutions. It was officially declared a Science City in 2000 because it houses several major research and educational institutions specializing in agriculture, biotechnology, and aquaculture.

Some key institutions in Muñoz that contribute to its "Science City" status include:

* [[Philippine Rice Research Institute|Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice)]] – Focuses on rice science and development.
* [[Central Luzon State University|Central Luzon State University (CLSU)]] – A top agricultural university.
* [[Philippine Carabao Center|Philippine Carabao Center (PCC)]] – Conducts research on water buffalo genetics and dairy production.
* [[Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization|Bureau of Postharvest Research and Extension (BPRE)]] – Works on improving postharvest technologies.
* National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) – Researches alternative energy sources.

==History==
===Early history===
The present-day city was formerly a ''[[barrio]]'' known as '''Papaya'''. In 1886, the name was changed to '''Muñoz''' in honor of Don Francisco Muñoz, the first appointed ''[[gobernadorcillo]]''.<ref name="pdi1100" />

The ''barrio'' was once a forested area. During [[American occupation of the Philippines|the American occupation]], in 1907, part of it was selected for the establishment of a government agricultural school—the present-day [[Central Luzon State University]] (CLSU).<ref name="pdi03sr">{{cite news |last=Roque |first=Anselmo |date=September 2, 2003 |title=Science City of Muñoz: expanding the frontiers in agri-development; seeking new partners |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B7ljAAAAIBAJ&dq=mu%C3%B1oz+philippines&pg=PA47&article_id=1917,32823356 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location=[[Makati]] |publisher= |access-date=January 18, 2025 |page=D4 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

Residents of ''barrios'' Muñoz and San Anton in [[Guimba|San Juan de Guimba]], and of Palusapis in [[Santo Domingo, Nueva Ecija|Santo Domingo]], later petitioned for them, along with the ''[[sitio]]s'' in [[Talavera, Nueva Ecija|Talavera]]—Kabisukulan, Rangayan, Rizal, Mataas-na-lupa, Siniguelas, Pukoc, Agricultura, and Pulong-maragol—to be organized into a separate [[Municipalities of the Philippines|municipality]]. On October 18, 1912, [[Newton W. Gilbert]], [[Governor-General of the Philippines|the island's acting Governor General]], issued ''Executive Order No. 72'' which created Muñoz as the twenty-fourth municipality of Nueva Ecija, with Barrio Muñoz designated as the [[Poblacion|seat of government]];<ref name="EO72">{{cite book |date=1913 |title=Executive orders and proclamations (1912) |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7ItEAQAAMAAJ&q=mu%C3%B1oz |location=[[Manila]] |publisher=Bureau of Printing |pages=185–188 |isbn= |access-date=January 15, 2025 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> the order took effect on January 1, 1913.<ref name="pdi1100" /><ref>{{cite book |date=1934 |title=Revised Administrative Code of the Philippine Islands 1934 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ukmuAAAAMAAJ&dq=papaya-mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija&pg=PA100 |location=[[Washington, D.C.]] |publisher=[[United States Government Printing Office]] |page=100 |isbn= |access-date=January 10, 2025 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> As mandated, a municipal hall and a school building was constructed.<ref name="EO72" />
<!---
===From Sitio to Barrio===
In 1886, Papaya was changed into 'Muñoz' to honor Don Francisco Muñoz, the province's alcalde mayor, and the community's first appointed gobernadorcillo. Muñoz was annexed as a barrio of San Juan de Guimba municipality. Settlers trickled in from Bulacan and the Ilocos Region, with Pangasinenses & Kapampangans. In 1911, Factoria (now San Isidro town), the provincial capital, was totally flooded. Muñoz was then considered a possible new capital of the province.

At about the same time, the people of Barrios Muñoz and San Antonio, also in San Juan de Guimba town, and Palusapis in Santo Domingo municipality, together with Sitios Kabisukulan, Rang-ayan, Mataas na Lupa, Siniguelas, Purok Agrikultura, and Pulong Maragul in Talavera town, were organizing themselves to be separated from their three respective municipalities to become a new independent municipality. They were prepared to construct a municipal hall and a school building for the emerging town.

===From Barrio to town and Science City===
{{unreferenced section|date=September 2014}}
On the recommendation of the Provincial Board of Nueva Ecija, then headed by Governor [[Isauro Gabaldon]], and with approval of then Acting Governor General Newton Gilbert, the organized barrios and sitios were granted independence as a regular municipality on January 10, 1913, under the name of Muñoz. The seat of the fledgling municipal government was positioned in erstwhile Barrio Muñoz. The municipality of Muñoz was born and steadily grew to become an agricultural Science City in the making.

A municipal hall, a church, and a small public market were erected in Lumang Bayan (now Poblacion North). A road linking the young Muñoz town with the national highway from Barangay Bacal, Talavera was constructed.--->

In the aftermath of a typhoon that hit [[Luzon]] on October 9–11, 1936, and caused floods, affecting the central and southwestern part with the province the hardest hit, 20 bodies were found at the agricultural school.<ref>{{cite news |date=October 13, 1936 |title=Known storm dead 193 as 654 missing |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kfVPAAAAIBAJ&dq=papaya-mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija&pg=PA1&article_id=2165,2023634 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |newspaper=[[The Evening Independent]] |location=[[St. Petersburg, Florida]] |publisher= |access-date=January 10, 2025 |page=1 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

===Japanese period===
In January 1945, the [[United States Army]] landed at [[Lingayen Gulf]]. This was opposed by the [[Imperial Japanese Army]]'s 14th Army under the command of Gen. [[Tomoyuki Yamashita]]; its 2nd Tank Division, which had been in [[Luzon]] since July 1944, was involved in tank battles in [[Pangasinan]] and Nueva Ecija, particularly Muñoz and [[Lupao]].<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Destroyed Japanese 2nd Tank Division on Luzon (gallery of photographs) |url=https://pacificwrecks.com/people/veterans/thien/luzon/tanks/index.html |website=Pacific Wrecks |location= |publisher=Pacific Wrecks Inc. |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

Gen. [[William Krueger]], realizing the strategic importance of capturing [[San Jose, Nueva Ecija|San Jose]] (situated in the municipality's northeast), ordered units under the [[I Corps (United States)|I Corps]] of the [[United States Army]] to liberate the area. The [[Empire of Japan|Japanese]] defense had eight strong points around the area, including that at Muñoz, which was ordered attacked by Gen. [[Innis Swift]], commander of the I Corps, to the 6th Division.<ref>{{cite web |last= |first= |date=n.d. |title=Liberation of San Jose, Nueva Ecija |url=https://pvao.gov.ph/events/liberation-of-san-jose-nueva-ecija/ |website=[[Philippine Veterans Affairs Office]] |location=[[Philippines]] |publisher=[[Department of National Defense (Philippines)|Department of National Defense]] |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref> Filipinos also engaged the Japanese in a close-quarter battle—the '''battle of Muñoz'''—including Col. Cesar Pobre, a member of the [[United States]] 98 Mortar Brigade.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cal |first=Ben |date=April 8, 2024 |title=966 Filipino WW2 veterans still alive — PVAO |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1222229 |work=[[Philippine News Agency]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

<!---In World War II, Muñoz was the last stronghold of the Japanese Imperial Army; the Allied liberation in Muñoz by the joint United States and Philippine Commonwealth forces offensive razed the town to the ground in a matter of days.

-----

In January 1945, following the [[Invasion of Lingayen Gulf|United States Army landing at Lingayen Gulf]], [[United States|American]] forces proceeded to capture [[San Jose, Nueva Ecija|San Jose]], aiming to cut the last land link between the [[Empire of Japan|Japanese]] battle groups defending the [[Northern Luzon|north]] and [[Southern Luzon|south Luzon]]. This involved the '''battle of Muñoz''', where the [[6th Infantry Division (United States)|6th Infantry Division]], which were among those arrived at the [[Lingayen Gulf]], was mostly involved and consisted of Company C, 44th Tank Battalion—shared with the [[1st Cavalry Division (United States)|1st Cavalry Division]]; Company A, 716th Tank Battalion—split among the 6th and [[43rd Infantry Division (United States)|43rd divisions]]; in addition to a detachment of the latter battalion's service company.<ref name="Bwt" />

In the other hand, at the same month after the American landing, the almost entire [[Imperial Japanese Army|Japanese Army]] 6th Tank Regiment was deployed in Muñoz with their 55 tanks deployed around the Agricultural School, as the town was guarded by the 356th Independent Infantry Battalion.<ref name="Bpwi" /> By end of the month,<ref name="Bpwi" /> the municipality became the largest Japanese strong point, being fortified by some 2,000 troops—also including the 2nd Tank Division.<ref name="Bwt" />

-----

On January 26, [[United States Army]] artillery began the bombardment in Muñoz; however, at first, the 6th Division, [[20th Infantry Regiment (United States)|20th Infantry Regiment]] failed at least thrice to advance towards the area, stalling its frontal attack.<ref name="Bpwi" /> One of these—the second—occurred at 7:30 a.m. of January 31, when Company K, 20th regiment, approaching the town from the southwest through a rail line, had its assault platoons being immobilized by the Japanese which had their installations hiding in the bomb-shattered buildings. Some elements of the 3rd Battalion moved up to company's line. No any movement was done for the next two days.<ref name="Bwt" />

On the other hand, on January 28, following the Japanese defeat at [[San Manuel, Pangasinan]], American forces began advancing toward Muñoz.<ref name="Bpwi" /> On February 1, Company C, 44th Tank Battalion, a platoon from the 716th Tank Battalion, and the 6th division troops came to the town.<ref name="Bwt" />

Meanwhile, two another American regiments bypassed Muñoz to reach San Jose,<ref name="Bwt" /> surrounding the former.<ref name="Bpwi" /> On February 2, the rest of Company C's tanks worked with the [[63rd Infantry Regiment (United States)|63rd Infantry Regiment]] did so; the 2nd Platoon finally crossed and destroyed the Japanese defenses, completely surrounding the latter's line.<ref name="Bwt" /> The said regiment occupied the Agricultural School.<ref name="Bpwi" /> On February 4, the [[1st Infantry Regiment (United States)|1st Infantry Regiment]] entered San Jose almost unopposed,<ref name="Bwt" /> liberating the area, and forming a roadblock towards Muñoz.<ref name="Bpwi" />

On February 3, the 20th Infantry broke the first Japanese line at the town's south, gradually capturing the town until the next three days. Meanwhile, Company B was fighting on the town's east.<ref name="Bwt" /> On February 5, 2nd Lt. [[Donald Rudolph]] successfully led the attack on the enemy positions (thus earning the [[Medal of Honor]]);<ref name="Bpwi" /> a Japanese position claimed a Company C tank.<ref name="Bwt" />

By February 6, withdrawal orders reached the Japanese defenders;<ref name="Bwt" /> leading them to an escape attempt to already American-occupied San Jose until the morning of the next day,<ref name="Bwt" /><ref name="Bpwi" /> but were suppressed by artillery fire from the U.S. 53rd and 58th Field Artillery Battalions.<ref name="Bpwi" /> Some infantry reached the hills.<ref name="Bpwi" />

At the end, the Japanese force suffered 1,500 [[killed in action]]; the Americans, 90 killed and 550 [[Wounded in action|wounded]].<ref name="Bpwi">{{cite web |date= |title=Munoz (Muñoz) |url=https://pacificwrecks.com/location/philippines_munoz.html |website=Pacific Wrecks |location= |publisher=Pacific Wrecks Inc. |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref> The Japanese 6th Tank Regiment lost 52 [[tank]]s,<ref name="Bwt" /><ref name="Bpwi" /> 41 trucks,<ref name="Bpwi" /> four armored cars,<ref name="Bwt" /> sixteen 47mm [[anti-tank gun]]s, and four 105mm [[howitzer]]s.<ref name="Bwt" /><ref name="Bpwi" /> By mid-March, Americans had destroyed 95% of the 2nd Tank Division, involving 222 tanks, mostly in the Muñoz-San Jose area.<ref name="Bwt">{{cite web |last=Yeide |first=Harry |date=May 3, 2015 |title=The Chieftain's Hatch: The Battle of Munoz [sic] |url=https://worldoftanks.com/en/news/history/chieftains-hatch-munoz/ |website=[[World of Tanks]] |location= |publisher=[[wargaming.net]] |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

-----

On January 21, the enemy, which had enveloped [[Tarlac City|Tarlac]] and [[Victoria, Tarlac|Victoria]], began going northeastward to Guimba and Muñoz, apparently to outmaneuver the 2nd Armored Division's main positions on the [[Tayug]]–Triangle Hill line and attack them at [[San Jose, Nueva Ecija|San Jose]] from the southwest. Seeing that the division's reinforcement—the almost entire 6th Tank Regiment at the Muñoz sector, which had been shifted a day prior, was not enough for their defense; on January 26, the Area Army ordered a rearrangement among the division, removing their strength at the Tayug–[[Umingan]] and Triangle Hill sectors to concentrate its forces in an area bounded by Lupao, Muñoz, and [[Rizal, Nueva Ecija|Rizal]], with main positions on Highways 8 (Lupao–San Jose) and 5 (Muñoz–San Jose).<ref name="dm94" />

On the Muñoz front (southwest of San Jose), a battle occurred, fiercer than that at [[San Manuel, Pangasinan|San Manuel]]. The Ida Detachment had been there on January 25, when the enemy began preliminary attacks to enter their defenses. On February 1, enemy forces launched a full-scale assault on Muñoz from the southwest.<ref name="dm94" />

The Ida Detachment had positioned itself in strong defensive positions. The assault made no progress on February 1–2. (On the 3rd, however, enemy forces by-passed Munoz on the southeast and cut in behind the Ida Detachment to sever Highway 5 in the vicinity of the [[Central Luzon State University|Central Luzon Agricultural School]], between Munoz and [[San Jose, Nueva Ecija|Santo Tomas]]). They then advanced toward San Jose. Enemy elements again turn around the Japanese positions to go to San Jose on February 4. By February 6, Highway 5 (Agricultural School–San Jose) was under the enemy.<ref name="dm94" />

The Ida Detachment cut still holding its positions. Col. Kumpei Ida, its commander, had already been [[killed in action]]. By February 6, the enemy only gained possession of only a portion of the town.<ref name="dm94" />

On February 4, the Area Army issued the order to the 2nd Armored Division to withdraw northward, only to reach the headquarters until February 6 due to communications failure.<ref name="dm94" />

At that time, the enemy seizure of San Jose had already blocked the escape route of the division forces at Muñoz and along Highway 8 ([[Lupao|Lupao–San Isidro]]).<ref name="dm94" />

The Ida Detachment chose to attempt a retreat, breaking through the enemy blocking their route. The remaining strength pulled out of Munoz about midnight on the 6th, heading up Highway 5 toward San Jose.<ref name="dm94" />

The attempt was later discovered. Between the Agricultural School and Santo Tomas, enemy weapons attacked the column, causing heavy casualties and destroying virtually all equipment.<ref name="dm94" />

Surviving personnel, after destroying their remaining vehicles, scattered around San Jose toward the advance positions of the 10th Division between Lupao and San Isidro.<ref name="dm94">{{cite book |last=MacArthur |first=Douglas |author-link=Douglas MacArthur |date=1994 |title=Reports of General MacArthur: Japanese operations in the Southwest Pacific area (Volume II — Part II) |chapter=Chapter XV — Battle on Luzon |url=https://www.history.army.mil/books/wwii/MacArthur%20Reports/MacArthur%20V2%20P2/ch15.htm |location=[[Washington, D.C.]] |publisher=[[United States Department of the Army]] |pages=477–482 |isbn= |access-date=January 20, 2025 |via=[[United States Army Center of Military History]]}}</ref>
---->

===Post-colonial period===
Muñoz had its territory reduced on January 1, 1948, when ''barrios'' Alula, Calisitan, and Saverona were separated and, along with portions of [[Cuyapo]], Guimba, and Lupao, were organized into the province's twenty-eighth municipality—[[Talugtug]]—by virtue of Executive Order No. 113.<ref>{{cite PH act |title=Establishment of the municipality of Talugtug in the province of Nueva Ecija |chamber=EO |number=113 |folio= |language= |date=December 20, 1947 |url=https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1947/eo_113_1947.html |access-date=January 21, 2025 |ref=}}</ref>

In late September of that year, a ten-hour battle, one of the bloodiest between the [[Philippine Constabulary]] (PC) and the [[Hukbalahap]], occurred near the municipality where 83 people were killed.<ref>{{cite news |date=September 25, 1948 |title=83 Killed in Battle |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7xENAAAAIBAJ&dq=mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija+during+world+war+ii&pg=PA2&article_id=4814,4845620 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |location=[[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]] |publisher= |access-date=January 15, 2025 |page=2 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

During [[Presidency of Ferdinand Marcos|the Marcos administration]] [[Fourth Philippine Republic|post-martial law]], Jun Quimpo, [[Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos|an activist]] who had been working for an underground movement in the rural areas, [[Human rights abuses of the Marcos dictatorship|was fatally shot]] by his former comrade who had surrendered to the PC, in Calisitan in December 1981.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pedroso |first1=Kate |last2=Medina |first2=Marielle |date=September 1, 2015 |title=Never too young to be heroes — Liliosa Hilao: First Martial Law detainee killed |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/718061/liliosa-hilao-first-martial-law-detainee-killed |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location= |publisher= |access-date=January 20, 2025}}</ref>

The municipality was affected by the [[1990 Luzon earthquake]]; with 75 people died in the collapse of the library of the CLSU.<ref>Citations:
* {{cite news |last=Roque |first=Anselmo |date=July 20, 2001 |title=Quake scars won't leave Ecija highway |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=haU2AAAAIBAJ&dq=munoz+nueva+ecija+earthquake&pg=PA15&article_id=837,1543782 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location=[[Makati]] |publisher= |access-date=January 10, 2025 |page=A15 |via=[[Google Books]]}}
* {{cite news |last=Fabonan |first=Epi III |date=July 17, 2016 |title=#Journeyto30 — Earthquake! |url=https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2016/07/17/1603676/journeyto30-earthquake |newspaper=[[The Philippine Star]] |location= |access-date=January 10, 2025}}</ref>

In September 1993, through the initiatives of the leadership of the municipality and the CLSU,<ref name="pdi03sr" /> the agricultural town became the fifth in the country to be classified by the [[Department of Science and Technology (Philippines)|Department of Science and Technology]] (DOST) as a science community.<ref name="pdi1100" /><ref name="MpdiN" /><ref name="MpdiD" /> This is due to the presence of various [[centers of excellence]] and [[research and development]] agencies;<ref name="MpdiN" /> at the time of the cityhood, there were sixteen, most notably the CLSU, [[Philippine Rice Research Institute]], [[Philippine Carabao Center]], as well as the provincial offices of the DOST and the [[Agricultural Training Institute]].<ref name="pdi1100" /><ref name="pdi03sr" />

===Cityhood===
Mayor Efren Alvarez (who would be the first city mayor; served 1992–2001)<ref name="ps13" /> later sought the conversion of the municipality into what would be the country's first ''"Science City."''<ref name="ms0896" /> A master plan was then developed for the development into such agricultural entity.<ref name="pdi03sr" /> The [[Nueva Ecija Provincial Board]] endorsed the cityhood through a resolution. However, [[Nueva Ecija's 2nd congressional district|the province's second district representative]] Eleuterio Violago said that the requirements for cityhood were yet to be complied.<ref name="ms0896">{{cite news |last=Giray |first=Celso |date=August 17, 1996 |title='Science City' dream |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=amwVAAAAIBAJ&dq=mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija&pg=PA8&article_id=4221,2546017 |newspaper=[[Manila Standard]] |location=[[Manila]] |publisher= |access-date=January 9, 2025 |page=8 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

Nevertheless, in 1998, the cityhood bill was sponsored in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] by Simeon Garcia (Violago's successor), being supported by [[Governor of Nueva Ecija|provincial governor]] [[Tomas Joson III]];<ref name="pdi03sr" /> and was co-introduced by Josefina Joson, [[Legislative districts of Nueva Ecija|also from the province]].<ref name="pdi1100" /> It was later sponsored in the [[Senate of the Philippines|Senate]] by senators [[Sergio Osmeña III]] and [[Vicente Sotto III]]. According to senator [[Aquilino Pimentel Jr.]], [[Philippine Senate Committee on Local Government|the chamber's local government]] chairperson, the bid was different as it was about the creation of a city of such kind, being passed by the House prior to adoption by the Senate of a ruling that was supposed to make the plan be rejected.<ref name="pdi1100" />

On November 7, 2000, President [[Joseph Estrada]] signed [[Republic Act]] No. 8977,<ref name="MpdiN" /> converting the town into a ''science city'', which is also the world's second after [[Tsukuba]], [[Japan]].<ref name="pdi1100">{{cite news |last=Roque |first=Anselmo |date=November 14, 2000 |title=RP's first science city born in Ecija |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oVg1AAAAIBAJ&dq=papaya-mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija&pg=PA12&article_id=3671,22678987 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location=[[Manila]] |publisher= |access-date=January 10, 2025 |page=A12 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> On December 9, the conversion was ratified in a plebiscite with about 12,468 voters favoring the bid, against 602 who voted against; hence becoming the province's fourth [[Cities of the Philippines|component city]],<ref name="MpdiD" /> officially bearing the name '''Science City of Muñoz'''<ref name="MpdiN">{{cite news |last=Adalid |first=Nathalie Grace |date=November 3, 2024 |title=This week's milestones: Nov. 3 to Nov. 9 |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2000576/this-weeks-milestones-nov-3-to-nov-9 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location= |access-date=January 9, 2025}}</ref><ref name="MpdiD">{{cite news |last=de Villa |first=Kathleen |date=December 3, 2017 |title=This Week's Milestones: Dec. 3–9 |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/949330/this-weeks-milestones-philippine-history-6 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location= |access-date=January 31, 2018}}</ref>—the only local government unit in the country holding such designation to date.<ref name="pna23" />

<!---Thereafter, universities and scientific research institutes sprung up. The local government adopted and later ratified the Science city moniker.--->

===Contemporary===
Muñoz is among those areas in the province's northwest whose [[rice field]]s are being reached by the Casecnan Multi-Purpose Irrigation and Power Project of the [[National Irrigation Administration]]; the project became operational in 2001.<ref>Citations:
* {{cite news |last=Roque |first=Anselmo |date=September 19, 2001 |title=Casecnan: A river of many returns |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PqhjAAAAIBAJ&dq=munoz+nueva+ecija+earthquake&pg=PA16&article_id=1601,37668239 |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location=[[Makati]] |publisher= |access-date=January 10, 2025 |page=A16 |via=[[Google Books]]}}
* {{cite news |last=Galang |first=Armand |date=February 26, 2008 |title=Nueva Ecija irrigation project starts operation, releases water to farmlands |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EU5aAAAAIBAJ&dq=mu%C3%B1oz+nueva+ecija&pg=PA7&article_id=1764,5746632 |newspaper=[[The Manila Times]] |location=[[Manila]] |publisher= |access-date=January 9, 2025 |page=A7 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

At the early morning of September 26, 2012, a [[traffic collision]] occurred on [[Maharlika Highway]] in Barangay Bantug, killing the drivers of a [[Victory Liner]] bus and a fuel tanker, five bus passengers, and a couple on a motorcycle.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roque |first1=Anselmo |last2=Galang |first2=Armand |date=September 27, 2012 |title=Nueva Ecija bus, motorcycle, tanker crash: 9 killed, 8 hurt |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/278098/nueva-ecija-bus-motorcycle-tanker-crash-9-killed-8-hurt |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location= |access-date=January 9, 2025}}</ref>

In November 2012, mayor Alvarez and vice mayor Ester Lazaro had a dispute over the mayorship<ref>{{cite news |last=Galang |first=Armand |date=February 27, 2013 |title=Nueva Ecija city has no mayor as court issues warrant |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/366041/nueva-ecija-city-has-no-mayor-as-court-issues-warrant |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |location= |access-date=January 9, 2025}}</ref> as the latter was designated as acting mayor.<ref name="ps13" /> In February 2013, the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]] unseated Alvarez after affirming his 2009 conviction by the [[Sandiganbayan]] for [[Graft (politics)|graft]].<ref name="ps13">{{cite news |last=Punay |first=Edu |date=February 9, 2013 |title=SC upholds conviction for graft of Ecija mayor |url=https://www.philstar.com/nation/2013/02/09/906470/sc-upholds-conviction-graft-ecija-mayor |newspaper=[[The Philippine Star]] |location= |access-date=January 9, 2025}}</ref>

On August 22, 2023, Muñoz and [[Batac]] signed a [[Sister city|sisterhood agreement]].<ref name="pna23">{{cite news |last=Adriano |first=Leilanie |date=August 22, 2023 |title=Nueva Ecija's Muñoz, Ilocos Norte's Batac forge sister ties |url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1208311 |work=[[Philippine News Agency]] |location= |access-date=January 9, 2025}}</ref>

==Geography==
[[File:Ph locator nueva ecija munoz.png|thumb|270px|Previous Muñoz map in December 20, 2008]]
Muñoz is situated {{convert|30|km}} from [[Cabanatuan]], {{convert|44|km}} from [[Palayan]], and {{convert|146|km}} north of the capital [[Manila]]. Due to its rich topography and tropical climate, it is now home to agricultural research and technology centers, committed to the production of information and technological breakthroughs to promote rural development, productivity, and [[food security]].

===Dispute===
The National Government has an ongoing move to transfer the Talavera barangays of Matingkis (Talavera), Bakal 1, Bakal 2 and Bakal 3 to become part of Science City of Munoz for the reason that the said barangays are geographically and strategically within the said city. This was favored by most of the residents of the said barangays but opposed by the Municipal Government of Talavera.

Also there is a proposed separation of Villa Pinili (Bantug West) and San Juan (CLSU) which will include PNR (CLSU), and Sawmill (CLSU) from Barangay Bantug into two independent separate barangays.

== Economy ==
{{stack|float=left|{{PH poverty incidence}}}}
[[File:Pccfacadejf.JPG|thumb|right|Philippine Carabao Center facade, National Headquarters and Gene Pool]]
[[File:Mango Grove, Nueva Ecija.jpg|thumb|right|Mango grove in Muñoz]]
There are many new establishments in Munoz in the past few years. Notable are Jollibee Munoz, Mang Inasal Munoz, 7/11, BDO, Land Bank, Novo, Lucky 99, Friendship Supermarket, Inc (FSi), and the Villa-Mendoza Training Institute, are now major landmarks on the city.

In terms of commercial and shopping sector, [[Robinsons Malls|Robinsons]], [[Savemore Market|Savemore]] and [[Puregold]] has also initially identified locations in the city for future construction. Fast-food chain operator [[Jollibee]] already established their store in the city.

With a bustling market center with rice trading as a major economic activity, it has transformed into its present status as a Science City by virtue of Republic Act 8977 on December 9, 2000. Being a science city, Muñoz was acknowledged as one of the members of [[League of Cities of the Philippines]] and became a pilot city of achieving the United Nation's [[Millennium Development Goals]].

;Research and development centers:
*The Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) (formerly the Maligaya Rice Research and Training Center (MRRTC)) is found in Muñoz
*Central Office and National Genepool of the Philippine Carabao Center (PCC). 
*National Freshwater and Fisheries Training and Research Center (NFFTRC)
*The main offices of the Bureau of Postharvest Research and Extension (BPRE) now known as Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PhilMech) 
*Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR-NFFTC) are also based in Muñoz.

==Education==
*[[Central Luzon State University]] - a state university located on a 658-hectare campus. It serves as the lead agency of the Muñoz Science Community and hosts the Regional Research and Development Center in Central Luzon. CLSU is recognized for its significant contributions to agricultural research in Southeast Asia, particularly in areas such as aquatic culture (notably in the sex reversal of tilapia), ruminant studies, crop science, orchard management, and water management.<ref name="fitzsimmonsAZ">{{cite web | last = Fitzsimmons | first = Kevin | title = Tilapia Aquaculture in the Philippines | url = https://ag.arizona.edu/azaqua/philippines/clsu.htm | access-date = 3 June 2024 | website = The University of Arizona College of Agriculture & Life Sciences}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.agribusinessweek.com/update-on-tilapia-sex-reversal/|title=Update On Tilapia Sex Reversal|publisher=Agriculture Business Week| url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100728205722/http://www.agribusinessweek.com/update-on-tilapia-sex-reversal/| archive-date = 28 July 2010 }}</ref>
